historical_water_holding_evidence.evidence: The recorded hours-long water hold belongs to the Basic material recipe. It is not a Translucent result.

material_and_recipe_evidence.selected_float_process: The float uses the reservoir's current Translucent Clear material, with sealing temperature, flow and low-cooling choices adapted from the recorded Basic recipe. Translucent's native 16 mm³/s volumetric ceiling is retained.
material_and_recipe_evidence.calculation_implications: Use Translucent-specific material references. Its density remains 1.25 g/cm³. Its XY Young's modulus is 1420 MPa and its distinct XY flexural modulus is 1610 MPa; neither is a measured float allowable.

decisions.classification: manufacturer cycles with engineering workflow selection
decisions.selected: Complete ASA Aero 80 °C × 8 h in AMS HT and PETG Translucent Clear 32101 65 °C × 12 h in AMS 2 Pro using static drying. Keep each spool in its sealed unit for normal feeding after drying.
decisions.engineering_reason: Uses acquired equipment without a transfer or bypass path. Completing the cycle avoids depending on reduced-temperature drying during printing.

decisions.classification: manufacturer preparation with one owned adhesive selected
decisions.selected: Wash and dry both plates. Apply a thin even layer of the owned Bambu liquid glue to the Engineering plate for Aero. Print the PETG shell on clean Textured PEI using its supplied recipe.
decisions.engineering_reason: Liquid glue is explicitly inventoried. The PETG plate choice follows the successful reservoir recipe.

decisions.classification: manufacturer filament preset and guide process, with float-specific geometry settings
decisions.selected: Print core plate 1, then insert plate 2, at 270 °C nozzle, 90 °C Engineering bed, 60 °C chamber and 0.52 flow through the right 0.4 mm standard-flow nozzle. Keep the enclosure closed and run shop ventilation or extraction.
decisions.scope_note: The supplied core uses solid foamed fill; that geometry setting is a project choice.

decisions.classification: official PETG plate release temperature; conservative engineering threshold for Aero and changeover
decisions.selected: Keep the enclosure closed for the initial Aero cooldown. Remove each finished part only at a bed temperature of 35 °C or lower, flexing the sheet gently. Before PETG, cool the chamber to 35 °C or lower.
decisions.scope_note: Bambu explicitly specifies ≤35 °C for Textured PEI removal. Applying the same threshold to Aero on Engineering plate and to chamber changeover is our handling choice, not a manufacturer Aero specification. No fixed cooling duration is claimed.

decisions.classification: manufacturer component facts with engineering assembly inference
decisions.selected: Preload one room-temperature RC62 into the cooled core on the bench, with its flat faces horizontal and its hole coaxial with the core bore. Either flat face may face upward for the single-magnet, unbiased MDSR-7 arrangement.
decisions.scope_note: Either-face-up follows the Form A reed's response to either field polarity. It does not imply identical thresholds in an externally biased field or specify an orientation for a different sensor.

decisions.classification: local project parameters and engineering thermal handling
decisions.selected: Use left 0.6 mm standard-flow PETG Translucent Clear 32101 at 255/260 °C nozzle, 70 °C bed, 1.02 flow and a 16 mm³/s volumetric ceiling. Keep chamber heating off. At the programmed pause, leave the sheet mounted and the bed at 70 °C; insert the preloaded core and upper insert, remove the tool, close the enclosure and resume promptly.
decisions.scope_note: The sealing overrides are an engineering adaptation from the historical Basic recipe, not a documented Translucent water-hold result. The project pauses with M400 U1; the printer manages nozzle temperature on resume. Room-temperature inserts and a ready tool shorten the pause.

decisions.selected: Trim brims and loose strings mechanically. Keep the foam dry. The finished assembly needs no glue joint, cure cycle, anneal or post-bake.
decisions.engineering_reason: The printed closure and mechanical insert fit complete the assembly; the RC62 has an 80 °C service-temperature limit.

printable_steps: Dry ASA Aero White in the AMS HT at 80 °C for 8 hours. Dry PETG Translucent Clear 32101 in the AMS 2 Pro at 65 °C for 12 hours. Run both overnight; leave the spools sealed in their units.
Fit the right 0.4 mm standard-flow induction nozzle and left 0.6 mm standard-flow nozzle. Connect ASA's AMS HT to the right feed and PETG's AMS 2 Pro to the left feed.
Wash and dry the Engineering plate. Apply a thin even layer of Bambu liquid glue. Open the Aero project and retain its supplied settings.
Print Aero plate 1, then plate 2: 270 °C nozzle, 90 °C bed, 60 °C chamber. Keep the enclosure closed and ventilation running. Cool each part to a bed temperature of 35 °C or below before release.
Trim the Aero brims and loose strings. Press one RC62 into the cooled core's magnet pocket on the bench. Lay out that core, the upper insert and the insertion tool.
Cool the chamber to 35 °C or below. Fit the clean dry Textured PEI plate. Open the PETG shell project, retain its supplied settings and start the shell.

At the programmed pause, keep the plate mounted and the bed at 70 °C. Seat the preloaded core and upper insert using the guide's tool sequence. Remove the tool, close the enclosure and resume promptly.
Let the closed float cool to a bed temperature of 35 °C or below. Flex the plate gently to release it, then remove its brim and loose strings.
